properties.comments: NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph tracked from Treasure Isle in southeast St. Tammany Parish to rural parts of southwest Hancock County, north of Pearlington. The tornado began near or before moving into Treasure Isle where it flipped a large boat on its side. Additional visible damage to homes and lofting of outdoor fixtures was noted as the tornado moved into Martin Drive. The tornado reached EF-1 intensity near Bluegill Drive where it removed shingles off of homes, snapped a few trees, and collapsed garage door structures and blew out a wall or two as a result in two different homes. A defined damage path was observed on LA Hwy 433 and then crossed into inaccesible marsh areas. A weak tornado debris signature was evident on KHDC and is the basis for connecting this damage to Avery Estates. The tornado continued northeast into Avery Estates where minor metal roof damage and tree damage was noted on Avery Drive and Smokey Hollow Drive. The tornado evidently strengthened and grew in size to around 300 yards in width as it moved just south of the northern part of Avery Drive and into US Hwy 190 where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. Several outbuildings were damaged and tension cables on a cell tower were snapped. It's possible the tornado slowed in this area as it pivoted and turned more to the east per KHDC radar imagery. Along US Hwy 190 a manufactured home had most of its roof removed and it was shifted significantly off its foundation. The tornado then moved into Pearl River Basin, inaccessible to ground survey. The tornado evidently maintained strength or even strengthened further over this area, evidenced by the deepening of a tornado debris signature lofted over 5000 feet. Tree damage was found by ground survey team on rural roads of southwest Hancock County as the tornado began to weaken and lift back to the northeast. The tornado is estimated to have lifted near or after Point Road prior to reaching MS Hwy 607.

An EF1 tornado touched down on the east bank of the MS River and moved northeast to the University of New Orleans. Damage across the city was mostly tree damage and minor building damage. Additional analysis, points and information will be added later. Additional changes are possible.
A NWS survey team concluded an EF-0 tornado produced damage to trees, several homes, and several electrical wooden poles in the McCord area of Houma. Time estimated by radar.

The tornado first touched down just northwest of the intersection of King Bee Rd and Ten Mile Church Rd. The tornado uprooted trees at a residence at Spiers Rd and King Bee Rd. The tornado intensified and likely reached its maximum intensity as it moved northeast toward Flint Creek Road. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. In addition, the roof was torn off of a residence and a mobile home, and roof damage was observed to several sheds and outside storage buildings. The tornado continued northeast and weakened as it crossed John Willis Rd. The tornado briefly intensified again to EF-1 strength as it crossed Highway 26 where several trees were uprooted and snapped. The tornado weakened and lifted as it crossed Big Four Rd north of Highway 26.

After review of available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery, the beginning point of the tornado was adjusted westward. Additional adjustments in the track are possible in the coming weeks as more clear passes of high resolution satellite imagery become available.

A NWS survey team concluded that an EF-1 tornado tracked from the corner of Afton St and Richmond Ave towards Dixie Ave in Houma. A truck was tossed 30 feet and sustained significant damage. Multiple snapped and uprooted trees were observed.  Several homes sustained a partial loss of their roofs. One home had a collapsed carport. Time estimated by radar.

A NWS survey team concluded an EF-1 tornado tracked from Evelyn Ave towards Woodhaven Dr and Roberta Grove Blvd.  Several businesses in the Lynn Park Shopping Center (at the corner of Prospect Ave and Grand Caillou Rd) sustained damage to almost every window and had partially collapsed interior walls and their roof. HVAC equipment on the roof was thrown northward onto the ground from these businesses. 4 homes had partial to significant roof loss.  One home had an exterior wall collapsed.  Several carports were significantly damaged.

A NWS survey team concluded that an EF-1 tornado tracked northeast across Hancock and Harrison counties. Tree damage was widespread along the track including several large trees uprooted and snapped. Minor damage was done to several properties. Additional revisions via high resolution satellite analysis concluded the tornado began west of Standard Dedeaux Rd, north of Rock Hill Dedeaux Rd where it quickly strengthened into an EF-1 tornado and reached its peak width of 275 yards wide. The tornado then evidently weakened and the damage path become more intermittent until it reached the Wolf River where another swath of trees was rated low-end EF-1. The tornado damage path became intermittent once more after crossing the intersection of Cemetery and Steel Bridge Rd. The tornado then evidently reached its third peak as an EF-1 tornado as it crossed Cemetery Rd and MS Hwy 53 where swaths of trees were damaged and uprooted. The tornado then rapidly dissipated as it continued northeast and it's estimated to have lifted prior to reaching Herman Ladner Rd.

A brief EF0 tornado touched down in Eden Isle, LA and moved east. Widespread branches and tree debris was found in Eden Isle along with a few houses with minor damage. One house had a failure at the garage where the wind looks to have been pushed into the garage. The tornado damaged businesses right near I-10 as it crossed over with a few more homes damaged and trees down in Lakeshore Village. 

The widespread light damage across Eden Isle did make this a difficult track, especially track width, to find. The additional damage was likely inflow from straight line winds and/or debris that was swirling out of the tornado.

An EF0 tornado with winds of 85 MPH tracked north to south across Arabi, LA in St. Bernard Parish. This was confirmed via eyewitness videos, along with debris thrown to the SE and convergent debris in that direction. Almost all of the damage was shingles off well built homes, fence damage and large branches down. Three houses had a good part of their roof removed. Two were older houses, one built in the 50s. One house had a car port attached to the roof which is where the failure occurred. The third was abandoned and neighbors confirmed it also had extensive termite damage. That and rot was observed on the roof. Given that well built homes had minor damage and the damage on the three houses were from older roofs, the rating is an 85 MPH EF0.

A well-defined damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified on high-resolution satellite imagery over rural, inaccessible parts of southeast St. Charles Parish. The tornado touched down near Bayou des Allemands and tracked north-northwest over rural, inaccessible marshland. While the majority of damage along this path was marsh vegetation, a narrow swath of trees were evidently damaged/displaced which is the basis for its EF-0 rating. The tornado continued north-northwest with the narrow damage path becoming less defined with time. The tornado dissipated east of Bayou Gauche after being on the ground for over 3 miles.

An EF-1 tornado touched down over inaccessible areas west of Bayou Dularge and tracked northeast toward Crozier Drive. Predominantly minor to moderate patches of tree damage were visible on high resolution satellite imagery along its path which were collocated with a tornado debris signature on Climavision radar V014. Trees were more evidently displaced and damaged as the tornado exited the inaccessible marsh and forested areas and moved over Crozier Drive. A NWS survey team observed two homes on Crozier Drive that had significant roof loss and at least one exterior wall collapsed for both homes. The tornado continued northeast across Bayou Dularge Rd and into more inaccessible marsh and forest vegetation where more minor damage was evident on satellite imagery. The end point of this tornado is estimated and it's possible it extended further northeast though no conclusive evidence of damage was identified.

A brief EF1 tornado occurred in the McHenry area, beginning just southwest of Beech Road, tracking northeast across Beech Road and Hall Road. On the tornadoes short track, it caused an approximately 40-yard-wide swath of tree damage visible via both Sentinel 2 satellite imagery and broadcast media supplied damage photos. Most the damage was in the form of tree uproots and snaps, with only minor roofing damage to one of the homes on Hall Road. It is possible the tornado tracked further northeast; however additional clearer high resolution satellite imagery will be needed for any further track adjustments.

After reviewing available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery, it was determined a brief EF1 tornado occurred northeast of Whites Crossing, shortly after the first EF1 tornado had dissipated. This is also supported by a brief radar indicated tornado debris signature off of KMOB in this area. This tornado caused substantial tree damage primarily in forest after crossing Melton Hatten Road. The tornado lifted in the forest due north of Miles Cemetery Road. Additional adjustments in the track are possible in the coming days or weeks as clearer satellite passes and higher resolution satellite imagery become available.

Review of available satellite imagery revealed just enough foliage/tree damage within Squirrel Bayou to assign an EF0 tornado rating to this tornado. Satellite imagery revealed minor damage, and most of the track is estimated for its start and end points based on the presence of a radar tornado debris signature. Further adjustments are possible with this tornado as additional high resolution satellite imagery becomes available in the coming days and weeks.

A brief EF-0 tornado touched down just west of Highway 225 between Kilcrease Rd and Green Jordan Rd and lifted just east of Hwy 225. The tornado produced spotty tree damage. A couple of small pine trees were snapped with many other large limbs down. No structural damage was noted to the homes in the area. The damage also lined up in the exact location of the radar identified tornado debris signature. It's possible the tornado started further to the west than the starting point indicates. Satellite data will be used to update the start and end points as needed.

Review of available satellite imagery revealed substantial changes to the overall track and strength of this tornado. The tornado began just west of State Highway 225 near Soloman Lane, tracking north-northeast across Highway 225 and Green Jordan Road. It was here the tornado caused low end EF1 tree damage. As it continued northward, it once again reached Highway 225 where it dissipated.

Available satellite imagery revealed a short-lived EF1 tornado began along Bay Minette Creek, tracking eastward for just under a half mile. The tornado primarily caused scattered tree damage along its track through Buzbee Road, with the most noteworthy tree damage being west of Buzbee Road after moving onshore.

An EF-1 tornado tracked through parts of Avondale, LA in Jefferson Parish. This tornado began over inaccessible areas to ground survey team near the levees, near Bayou Verret. A clear path of tree damage was evident on high resolution satellite imagery spanning to at least 250 yards wide with numerous trees displaced. The damage path within this inaccessible area became weaker and less apparent as the tornado approached US Hwy 90. The tornado was at EF-0 intensity as it crossed US Hwy 90 into Avondale. As it tracked northeast, the tornado caused light home damage and snapped tree branches. The tornado restrengthened to low-end EF-1 intensity at George Street, rolling a single-wide manufactured home into another home which was the cause of the most significant structural damage. The manufactured home was thrown to the northeast with the frame being well bent. 2 people were injured as a result. Additional home damage was also found on Defourneaux Ln as the tornado began to weaken again. It's estimated that the tornado lifted after crossing Restlawn Park Cemetery, near Center Street.

NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado impacted areas near Bayou Cane and moved northeast across US Hwy 190 west of Lacombe, LA in St. Tammany Parish. The tornado touched down near the shore of Lake Pontchartrain or came ashore as a tornadic waterspout with evident damage to marsh vegetation and trees per high resolution satellite imagery. The tornado was at peak intensity west of Lemieux Blvd where ground surveyors observed a few snapped trees on Cane Bayou Access Trail. Additional tree damage occurred on private property including several uprooted trees and a few snapped trunks as well as visible damage to a shed. The tornado uprooted and partially snapped trees as it crossed the Tammany Trace Bike Trail. The tornado began to evidently weaken as it approached and crossed US Hwy 190 causing only minor tree damage north of the highway. The tornado is estimated to have lifted near Azalea St and Cane Bayou Ln.

An EF-0 tornado touched down near Megan Drive, off of Coteau Rd, in northeast Terrebonne Parish. This tornado caused predominantly tree damage with some additional visible roof and siding damage to a couple homes. This tornado continued into Lafourche Parish where trees were visibly damage/displaced near Bayou Blue Rd on high resolution satellite imagery. The tornado continued into inaccessible marsh areas northeast of Bayou Blue Rd. A tornado debris signature was evident on Climavision Radar V014 through the duration of this tornado with the TDS dissipating near Hollywood Canal.

An EF-0 tornado touched down near Bayou la Cache, east of Chauvin, LA in Terrebonne Parish and tracked northeast toward Montegut, LA. High resolution satellite imagery depicted a defined swath of tree damage beginning over inaccessible areas which aligned with a tornado debris signature on Climavision V014. The damage path grew to a maximum width of 200 yards and peaked in intensity over inaccessible forest west of Blue Jay St as it enroached on neighborhoods near Crochetville Rd. The tornado gradually weakened and decreased in size as it moved over southern parts of Montegut, near Crochetville Rd where mainly minor tree damage was noted. It is estimated that this tornado dissipated near Willow Aly and Bayou Terrebonne.

A defined damage path in inaccessible marsh areas due to a short-lived tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery. The existence of this tornado was corroborated by a brief tornado debris signature on V014 Climavision radar. Lafourche Parish emergency management relayed that a tree was downed on a private road where this tornado crossed and is the basis for the EF-0 rating of this tornado.

As the Bayou Gauche-Luling Tornado occluded and weakened, it quickly handed off to another EF-0 tornado that quickly strengthened and caused a defined damaged swath of minor tree damage over largely inaccessible areas northeast of Destrehan, near Interstate 310. The tornado evidently weakened and lifted before reaching Airline Hwy. This damage path aligned closely with a strong tornado vortex signature on TMSY and evident weak debris signature on KHDC.

The damage path of a brief EF-0 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery in northwest Harrison County. This tornado caused predominantly damaged to trees over inaccessible areas between West Wortham and McHenry roads. This focused damage path closely aligned with a strong tornado vortex signature that crossed through the area. The tornado apparently lifted as it crossed McHenry Rd as no other damage could be identified as the circulation lifted northward.

The tornado began along Howells Ferry rd near Grider rd as a weak EF-0 bringing down a couple branches resulting in minor damage across two properties. The tornado then continued southeast across Carlisle Dr and strengthened as it approached Central Blvd and Mississippi St. south of Howells Ferry Rd. Several large uprooted hardwood trees were noted within this area with  more widespread small to large branches snapped throughout several roads within the community. The tornado then continued east towards Moffett Rd as it likely moved along Moffett before resulting in a few sporadic uprooted trees near a water treatment plant on the north side of Moffett Rd. The tornado likely weakened as it destroyed two businesses signs before dissipating near Northview Dr.

NWS ground survey in addition to high resolution satellite analysis confirmed an EF-0 tornado tracked from northeast of Bayou Gauche to west of Luling, LA in St. Charles Parish. The tornado evident damaged a patch of trees on high resolution satellite imagery and additional damage to marsh vegetation was evident with brief, weak tornado debris signatures also present on KHDC during this time. The tornado continued bending northward in direction as it approached the Blouin Canal with a larger, well-defined tornado debris signature becoming more evident on approach. A large tree was visibly damaged/displaced on high res satellite imagery in addition to other minor tree damage noted near Santa Cruz Ct as the tornado began to weaken and lift. The only minor tree damage was noted by the ground surveyor in the location.
